title: Quantum Scattering Model of Dual Parallel Mach Zehnder Electro Optic Modulators: General Formalism, Impairments, and Applications to Frequency-Bin Photonic Quantum States
authors: Mar Yuste, Carlos R. Fernández Pousa, Javier Fraile Peláez, José Capmany
abstract: We present a quantum mechanical model of dual parallel Mach Zehnder electro-optic modulators (DPMZMs), derived using the quantum scattering formalism [1,2]. We obtain the complete, unrestricted transformation of single-photon and coherent input states through the DPMZM architecture, including independent radiofrequency drive conditions on each internal modulator, and recover the symmetric push pull operating point as an exact special case. We numerically evaluate the resulting frequency comb structure, quantify the device sensitivity to bias error, modulation-index imbalance, and RF noise, and use the model to design a DP-MZM-based frequency-bin qubit source, reporting its fidelity as a function of these impairments.
summary: The paper presents a general quantum scattering model for Dual Parallel Mach-Zehnder Modulators (DP-MZMs) to analyze their effect on single photons and coherent states. It quantifies how imperfections like bias error degrade the performance of these modulators when used as frequency-bin qubit sources. The results are crucial for designing high-fidelity photonic quantum information systems.
main_problem: To develop a comprehensive quantum-mechanical model for Dual Parallel Mach-Zehnder Electro-Optic Modulators (DP-MZMs) to accurately describe their action on non-classical light.
main_result: The model provides the complete, unrestricted unitary transformation for single-photon and coherent states, allowing quantification of performance degradation due to various physical impairments like bias error and I/Q imbalance.
method: The analysis employs the quantum scattering formalism by deriving stage-by-stage unitary operators that compose the entire device action. This is applied separately to single-photon creation operators and displacement operators for coherent states.
model_or_system: The physical system is a DP-MZM used as a frequency shifter/encoder in photonic quantum information. The model tracks the evolution of light fields through cascaded beamsplitters, phase modulators, and combiners using unitary scattering operators ($\hat{S}_{DP}$).
key_observables: Single-photon sideband click probability $|\hat{H}(q)|^2$, two-frequency-bin qubit fidelity ($F$), and image-sideband suppression ratio ($\varepsilon_{dB}$).
important_parameters: Modulation indices ($m_I, m_Q$), quadrature bias error ($\Delta\phi_P$), I/Q imbalance, and RF drive frequencies ($\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The model is general, accounting for non-ideal components; however, the final analysis often assumes classical RF drives (c-number parameters) or uses approximations like the BCH theorem.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device layout and frequency comb structure. Numerical results show single-photon sideband probabilities under varying modulation indices and quantify qubit fidelity degradation versus bias error.
paper_structure: The paper derives the general unitary transformation for both single-photon and coherent inputs, analyzes specific operating points (push-pull vs. quadrature), and then numerically evaluates performance metrics like fidelity using Monte Carlo simulations to assess noise sensitivity.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous quantum description of a key photonic component used in quantum communication protocols, directly impacting the feasibility assessment for building practical quantum hardware.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Layout of the DP-MZM device, showing the input/output external beamsplitters, the in- phase and quadrature internal MZIs with their branch phase modulators, and the quadrature bias phase shifter, together with the unitary operators representing each component.

Fig. 2. Frequency-domain representation of quantum scattering in the DP-MZM. An input carrier state at frequency ωₒ is transformed into a superposition of sidebands at ωₒ + qΩ, forming a frequency-comb structure whose amplitudes are set by the coherent interference of the in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) branches. Single-photon and coherent-state transformations are illustrated for the two input cases treated in Sections 3 and 4.
Figure 3 illustrates this comb structure numerically for a representative single-photon input, showing how sideband power redistributes as the modulation index increases.

Fig. 3 (numerical illustration). Normalized single-photon sideband click probability |H(q)|² vs. sideband order q for three modulation indices, ideal push-pull operation, ϕₘ = π/2, balanced 3- dB splitters.

Fig. 4. Side-by-side comparison of (a) the single-photon click-probability spectrum and (b) the coherent-state mean-photon-number spectrum (input amplitude α₀ = 2), for identical DP-MZM operating conditions (m = 1.2, ideal push-pull bias). The two envelopes coincide up to normalization, confirming Eq. (9).
